question: In Delaware, what is the minimum age and experience requirement to hold a CDL for driving intrastate only?
choice_a: 18 years old with 1 year of driving experience
choice_b: 21 years old with 1 year of driving experience
choice_c: 18 years old with no driving experience required
choice_d: 21 years old with 2 years of driving experience
explanation: The manual states a basic CDL requirement is to be 18 years of age with 1 year driving experience for driving intrastate.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Basic CDL Requirements

question: What age and experience are required to drive in interstate commerce or transport hazardous materials under a Delaware CDL?
choice_a: 21 years old with at least 1 year driving experience
choice_b: 18 years old with at least 1 year driving experience
choice_c: 19 years old with at least 2 years driving experience
choice_d: 21 years old with no driving experience required
explanation: The manual requires a driver to be 21 years of age with at least 1 year of driving experience to drive interstate commerce or to transport hazardous materials.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Basic CDL Requirements

question: Under what federal regulation must a Delaware CDL applicant be able to obtain medical certification?
choice_a: 49 CFR Part 391.41, Physical Qualifications for Drivers
choice_b: 49 CFR Part 172, Subpart F
explanation: Applicants must be able to obtain medical certification under the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations Part 391.41, Physical Qualifications for Drivers.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Basic CDL Requirements

question: A driver who cannot meet the 49 CFR 391.41 physical qualifications may be able to obtain what kind of Delaware CDL, and what does it exclude?
choice_a: An intrastate-only restricted CDL medical waiver, excluding transporting passengers or hazardous materials
choice_b: A full interstate CDL with no restrictions
choice_c: An intrastate-only waiver that still allows hazardous materials transport
choice_d: A temporary 90-day CDL valid only for straight trucks
explanation: The manual states such a driver may obtain a Delaware intrastate-only restricted CDL medical waiver, if otherwise qualified, excluding transporting passengers or hazardous materials.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Basic CDL Requirements

question: A Delaware CDL Class A is required for what type of vehicle combination?
choice_a: Any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed unit(s) exceeds 10,000 pounds
choice_b: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_c: Any vehicle designed to carry 16 or more passengers
choice_d: Any combination vehicle regardless of weight rating
explanation: CDL Class A is required for any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed unit(s) is in excess of 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Types of CDL

question: Which Delaware CDL class covers any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds?
choice_a: Class B
choice_b: Class A
explanation: CDL Class B is required for any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing a vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Types of CDL

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR under 26,001 pounds falls under CDL Class C only if it meets which additional condition?
choice_a: It is designed to transport 16 or more passengers including the driver, or it is used to transport hazardous materials requiring the vehicle to be placarded
choice_b: It has a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_c: It is towing a unit with a GVWR over 10,000 pounds
choice_d: It is registered for interstate commerce only
explanation: Class C covers such vehicles only if they are designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Types of CDL

question: Which endorsement is required for a driver, regardless of vehicle class, who hauls material designated hazardous under 49 U.S.C. 5103 requiring placarding under 49 CFR 172 Subpart F?
choice_a: Hazardous Materials (H)
choice_b: Tanker (N)
explanation: The Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement is required for any driver, regardless of vehicle class, who hauls material designated hazardous under 49 U.S.C. 5103 requiring placarding under 49 CFR 172 Subpart F.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: What does a Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle (X) endorsement show that a driver has passed?
choice_a: Both the tank vehicle and hazardous materials knowledge examinations
choice_b: Only the tank vehicle knowledge examination
choice_c: Only the hazardous materials knowledge examination
choice_d: A special skills test for double and triple trailers
explanation: The X endorsement shows the driver has passed the special knowledge examinations for both tank vehicles and hazardous materials, required for drivers of tank vehicles hauling placarded hazmat or waste.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: What tank capacity thresholds trigger the requirement for a Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement in Delaware?
choice_a: Individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_b: Individual rated capacity of more than 1,000 gallons only
choice_c: Aggregate rated capacity of 119 gallons or more only
explanation: The N endorsement is required for a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more, permanently or temporarily attached.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A Passenger (P) endorsement is required for drivers of a vehicle with a design capacity to carry how many people, including the driver?
choice_a: 16 or more
choice_b: 10 or more
explanation: Drivers who wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity to carry 16 or more people, including the driver, must add a passenger endorsement to their CDL/CLP.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Which three endorsements may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_a: Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N)
choice_b: Hazardous Materials (H), Tanker (N), and Double/Triples (T)
explanation: The manual specifies that the only endorsements that may be added to a CLP are Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N).
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A driver who wants to pull double or triple trailers with a Class A vehicle must obtain which endorsement after passing a special knowledge examination?
choice_a: Double and Triple Trailers (T)
choice_b: Tank Vehicle (N)
explanation: Class A drivers who wish to pull double or triple trailers must add the T endorsement after passing a special knowledge examination on the problems associated with pulling multiple trailers.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: What does restriction code (E) indicate on a Delaware CDL?
choice_a: No manual transmission, applied if the skills test was taken in an automatic-transmission vehicle
choice_b: No CMV with any type of air brakes
explanation: Restriction (E) means no manual transmission, applied when an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: Restriction code (K) is applied to a Delaware CDL under what circumstance?
choice_a: The applicant certifies their status as Non-Excepted Intrastate or Excepted Intrastate, restricting them from operating a CMV in interstate commerce
choice_b: The applicant fails the air brake knowledge test
choice_c: The applicant's skills test used a vehicle with a pintle hook connection
choice_d: The applicant has a medical variance on file
explanation: Restriction (K), Intrastate only, applies if the applicant certifies their status as Non-Excepted Intrastate or Excepted Intrastate, restricting them from operating a CMV in interstate commerce.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: When does restriction (L) get applied to a Delaware CDL or CLP?
choice_a: If the applicant does not take or fails the air brake component of the knowledge test, or performs the skills test in a vehicle not equipped with air brakes
choice_b: If the applicant takes the skills test in a vehicle with air-over-hydraulic brakes
choice_c: If the applicant is issued a CLP with a Passenger endorsement
choice_d: If the applicant is a Non-Excepted Interstate driver
explanation: Restriction (L), no air-brake-equipped CMV, applies if the applicant does not take or fails the air brake knowledge test component, or tests in a vehicle without air brakes.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: If a Delaware CLP is issued with a Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement, what restriction must it also carry?
choice_a: (X) No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
choice_b: (P) No passengers in a CMV bus
explanation: If a CLP is issued with a Tanker (N) endorsement, it must also contain the (X) No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle restriction, limiting the holder to empty, purged tanks only.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: If a Delaware CLP is issued with a Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsement, what restriction must also be included?
choice_a: (P) No passengers in a CMV bus
choice_b: (X) No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
explanation: The manual states if a CLP is issued with a Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsement, it must also contain a (P) No passengers in a CMV bus restriction.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: In Delaware, once the appropriate knowledge exams are passed, what fee is assessed before a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) is issued?
explanation: The manual states that once the appropriate knowledge exams are passed, a fee of $5.00 will be assessed and the CLP will be issued.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Procedures for Obtaining a CDL

question: How long must a Delaware applicant hold a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) before taking the CDL skills test?
choice_a: A minimum of 14 full days
choice_b: A minimum of 30 full days
choice_d: There is no minimum holding period
explanation: The manual states you must hold your CLP for a minimum of 14 full days before you are able to perform the CDL skills test.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Procedures for Obtaining a CDL

question: In what order must the three segments of the Delaware CDL skills test be taken and passed?
choice_a: Vehicle Inspection (Pre-Trip Inspection), Basic Control Skills, then On-Road Driving
choice_b: Basic Control Skills, On-Road Driving, then Vehicle Inspection
choice_c: On-Road Driving, Vehicle Inspection, then Basic Control Skills
choice_d: The three segments may be taken in any order
explanation: The three parts of the skills exam are the Pre-Trip Inspection, Basic Control Skills, and On-Road Driving, and each must be taken in that order and passed before moving to the next.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: After May 31, 2005, a CDL with a hazmat endorsement may not be issued unless the applicant has first done what?
choice_a: Undergone the TSA security threat assessment and obtained clearance
choice_b: Passed only the general knowledge test
choice_c: Held a CDL for at least 5 years
explanation: After May 31, 2005, no CDL with hazmat endorsement may be issued unless the applicant has first undergone the security threat assessment and obtained clearance from the TSA.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Special Cases

question: Which of the following would cause a Delaware applicant to be denied or lose a hazardous materials endorsement?
choice_a: Not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
choice_b: Holding a Class A CDL
explanation: The manual lists not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States as one of the grounds for denial or loss of a hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: What must a Delaware hazmat-endorsed driver do within 24 hours of certain disqualifying convictions or indictments?
choice_a: Notify and surrender the hazardous materials endorsement to the state that issued the CDL
choice_b: Retake the general knowledge test
choice_d: Report to the nearest DMV for a new photo
explanation: The manual states a hazmat endorsement holder must notify and surrender the hazardous materials endorsement to the state that issued the CDL within 24 hours of certain disqualifying convictions or indictments.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-9

question: For a first Major violation (such as operating a CMV with BAC of .04% or more) committed in a private passenger vehicle or CMV, how long is a Delaware CDL disqualified?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Six months
explanation: The manual states that if convicted of a Major violation, your CDL will be disqualified for one year for the first offense.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: How long is a Delaware CDL disqualified for a first Major violation that occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials?
choice_a: Three years
choice_b: One year
explanation: Your CDL will be disqualified for three years if the first Major violation occurs while operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: What is the disqualification for a second Major violation of a Delaware CDL?
choice_a: Disqualification for life
choice_b: Two years
explanation: If convicted of a second Major violation, the manual states your CDL will be disqualified for life.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: How long is a Delaware CDL disqualified after two Serious Traffic violations committed in a CMV within any three-year period?
choice_a: 60 days
choice_b: 30 days
explanation: If convicted of two Serious Traffic violations within a three-year period, the CDL will be disqualified for 60 days.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: How long is a Delaware CDL disqualified after three or more Serious Traffic violations committed in a CMV within any three-year period?
choice_a: 120 days
choice_b: 60 days
explanation: The CDL will be disqualified for 120 days if convicted of three or more Serious Traffic violations within any three-year period.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: Which of the following is classified as a Serious Traffic Violation in the Delaware CDL manual?
choice_a: Excessive speeding of 15 mph or more above the posted limit
choice_b: Operating a CMV with a BAC of .04% or higher
choice_c: Leaving the scene of an accident
choice_d: Using a CMV to commit a felony
explanation: Serious Traffic Violations include excessive speeding of 15 mph or more above the posted limit, along with reckless driving, improper lane changes, and following too closely, distinct from the Major violations list.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Serious Traffic Violations

question: For a first offense of violating an Out-of-Service Order in a CMV that is NOT hauling hazardous materials, what is the Delaware disqualification range?
choice_a: No less than 180 days nor more than 1 year
choice_b: No less than 90 days nor more than 6 months
choice_d: No less than 1 year nor more than 2 years
explanation: The manual states that for a first offense of violating an Out-of-Service Order in a CMV, the CDL will be disqualified for no less than 180 days or more than 1 year.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Violating Out-of-Service Orders

question: For a first offense of violating an Out-of-Service Order while transporting hazardous materials in a CMV, what is the Delaware disqualification range?
choice_a: No less than 180 days nor more than 2 years
choice_b: No less than 90 days nor more than 1 year
choice_c: No less than 1 year nor more than 3 years
explanation: The manual states that a first offense of violating an Out-of-Service Order while transporting hazardous materials results in disqualification of no less than 180 days nor more than 2 years.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Violating Out-of-Service Orders

question: For three or more Out-of-Service Order violations within any ten-year period, what is the Delaware CDL disqualification range?
choice_a: No less than 3 years nor more than 5 years
choice_b: No less than 1 year nor more than 3 years
choice_d: No less than 180 days nor more than 1 year
explanation: The manual states the CDL will be disqualified for no less than 3 years or more than 5 years for three or more Out-of-Service Order violations within any ten-year period.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Violating Out-of-Service Orders

question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes it illegal to operate a CMV in Delaware?
choice_a: .04% or more
choice_b: .08% or more
explanation: The manual states it is illegal to operate a CMV if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is .04% or more.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7
